summary: Sun-soaked hillside city with pastel facades, outstanding seafood, and a melancholic soul — Europe's best value capital.

restaurants.name: Belcanto
restaurants.description: Two Michelin-star restaurant by chef José Avillez. Modern Portuguese cuisine at its peak.

restaurants.name: Tasca do Chico
restaurants.description: Tiny fado restaurant in Bairro Alto — live fado music, petiscos and natural wine.

restaurants.name: Time Out Market
restaurants.description: Curated market hall with the city's best chefs under one roof — outstanding for solo diners.

restaurants.name: Solar dos Presuntos
restaurants.description: Old-school taberna beloved by politicians and bullfighters since 1976.

restaurants.name: A Cevicheria
restaurants.description: Chef Kiko's playful take on Peruvian-Portuguese fusion under a giant octopus sculpture.

restaurants.name: Taberna da Rua das Flores
restaurants.description: No menu — the waiter recites the day's catch. Come hungry and adventurous.

restaurants.name: Restaurante Vicente
restaurants.description: Alentejo wine estate's Lisbon outpost — exceptional charcuterie and slow-roasted meats.

restaurants.name: Pastéis de Belém
restaurants.description: The original custard tart since 1837. Queue at 7 AM; still fresh every 20 minutes.

restaurants.name: Zé da Mouraria
restaurants.description: Worker's taberna in the Mouraria — enormous portions, surly waiters, perfect bifanas.

restaurants.name: Casa de Pasto
restaurants.description: Modern petiscos in a gorgeous azulejo-tiled room in Príncipe Real.

restaurants.name: Guilty by Olivier
restaurants.description: Upscale burgers and cocktails from Michelin-starred chef Olivier da Costa.

restaurants.name: Cervejaria Ramiro
restaurants.description: No-frills seafood palace open since 1956 — pile on the gambas and percebes.

activities.name: Tram 28 Ride
activities.description: Rattle through Alfama and Graça on Lisbon's iconic yellow tram — buy ticket on board.

activities.name: Alfama Fado Walking Tour
activities.description: Evening guided walk ending in a traditional fado restaurant with dinner.

activities.name: Sintra Day Trip
activities.description: UNESCO village of palaces in the hills — Pena Palace and Quinta da Regaleira are unmissable.

activities.name: Belém Tower & Jerónimos
activities.description: Manueline masterpieces at the mouth of the Tagus — UNESCO heritage.

activities.name: Cascais Coastal Walk
activities.description: Cycle or walk the 8 km seafront promenade from Estoril to Cascais.

activities.name: LX Factory Sunday Market
activities.description: Hip market in a repurposed textile factory — books, vintage, and street food.

activities.name: Miradouro da Graça Sunset
activities.description: Best free sunset viewpoint — locals bring wine and cheese, tourists arrive late.

activities.name: MAAT Museum
activities.description: Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology on the riverfront — stunning building.

activities.name: Surf Lesson at Cascais
activities.description: Atlantic swells make Lisbon's coast Europe's surf capital. Beginners welcome.

activities.name: Azulejo Painting Workshop
activities.description: Paint your own traditional blue tile at a local studio in Alfama.

activities.name: Wine Tasting in Príncipe Real
activities.description: Natural wine bar crawl through Lisbon's most fashionable neighbourhood.

activities.name: Arrábida Natural Park
activities.description: Turquoise coves and white cliffs 40 km south of Lisbon — bring a picnic.

spots.name: Miradouro da Graça
spots.description: Locals' favourite viewpoint with terracotta rooflines and the castle.

spots.name: Rua Agosta Rosa, Alfama
spots.description: Laundry-strewn alley with azulejo tiles and fado-house doorways.

spots.name: Tram 28 on Rua da Graca
spots.description: Catch the yellow tram cresting the hill — use a 70-200mm from distance.

spots.name: Belém Tower from the River
spots.description: Hire a kayak or take the ferry for a clean riverside composition.

spots.name: Pena Palace, Sintra
spots.description: Colourful Romanticist palace emerging from misty forest — ethereal at dawn.

spots.name: LX Factory Murals
spots.description: Ever-changing street art on derelict factory walls — new murals every season.

spots.name: Chiado from Rua Serpa Pinto
spots.description: Classic uphill view of church facades and wrought-iron balconies.

spots.name: Arrábida Limestone Cliffs
spots.description: Drone-perfect white cliffs over Caribbean-blue water. Check regulations.

spots.name: Mercado da Ribeira Interior
spots.description: Arched iron structure with perfect symmetry — wide angle essential.

spots.name: Santa Luzia Viewpoint Tiles
spots.description: Panoramic azulejo murals depicting old Lisbon — irresistible detail shots.

photography.goldenHourNotes: Lisbon faces west — the light hits the hilltop miradouros beautifully every evening. Morning fog sometimes clings to the valleys between the seven hills, creating layered cityscape shots.

weather.seasonality: Spring and early autumn are ideal — warm, uncrowded, and great light. July–August is peak season with 30°C+ heat and long queues. Winter is mild but rainy.
weather.summary: One of Europe's sunniest capitals. Mild winters, warm and dry summers. Best visited April–June or September–October.

hotels.name: Bairro Alto Hotel
hotels.description: Lisbon's most prestigious address — rooftop bar with 360° city views.

hotels.name: The Lumiares Hotel
hotels.description: Converted 18th-century palace with apartment-style suites and a rooftop pool.

hotels.name: Home Lisbon Hostel
hotels.description: Award-winning hostel in the heart of the city — legendary communal dinners.
